title: Formula (CSV / XLSX) injection via exported user input
summary: Prove user-controlled text reaches a generated spreadsheet or document cell without neutralizing a formula trigger, so a spreadsheet client would execute it on open. A reflected value that is quote-prefixed or escaped is not impact.
steps: Find a field whose value flows into an export or document-generation sink (CSV/XLSX download, invoice/report generation, PDF conversion).
Store a benign canary beginning with a formula trigger (=, +, -, @, a leading tab or CR), for example =1+1 or a harmless =HYPERLINK canary — never a data-exfiltration, DDE, or command formula.
Trigger the export and download the generated file (execute_curl / execute_browser), then inspect the target cell.
PASS if the cell retains the raw trigger prefix with no leading single quote, escaping, or stripping, so a spreadsheet client would evaluate it.
Change one variable at a time (field, trigger character); one canary cell is enough — do not seed many rows or production records.
On PASS: show the submitted value and the raw exported cell with evidence. KILL if the export prefixes a quote, escapes, or removes the trigger characters.
pass_signals: The exported cell keeps the raw formula prefix unescaped
kill_signals: The export quote-prefixes, escapes, or strips the trigger characters
